requirement_groups.name: Concentration 36 units
requirement_groups.source_instruction: Complete at least 36 units (a minimum of four courses) from the following concentrations of courses. Students are required to declare a concentration before their graduating semester, but are not required to choose a concentration when they initially declare (typically in the freshman or sophomore year). In fact, students are encouraged to take many of the core classes before making their concentration selection so that they can make a well-informed decision. Some courses have additional prerequisites.

requirement_groups.name: Concentration 36 units
requirement_groups.source_instruction: The Major in Policy and Management Peter Schwardmann, Faculty Director Location: Porter Hall 319F schwardmann@cmu.edu Connie Angermeier, Senior Academic Program Manager and Advisor Location: Porter Hall 208H cla2@andrew.cmu.edu Schedule an appointment: https://go.oncehub.com/ConnieAngermeier https://www.cmu.edu/dietrich/sds/undergraduate/policy-and-management/index.html Overview Great organizations do not succeed by accident. They depend on policymakers, managers, and other leaders who can bring together people, evidence, and strategy to solve difficult problems. The Policy and Management major prepares students for exactly those roles by combining scientific analysis, strategic thinking, negotiation, and policy expertise, equipping them to address complex challenges facing businesses, governments, nonprofits, healthcare systems, and other organizations. Students learn how to develop effective strategies, negotiate among competing interests, evaluate evidence, communicate across multiple stakeholders, and lead organizations through uncertainty and change. They learn why good ideas often fail in practice and how effective leaders translate evidence into action while balancing economic, political, and organizational realities. Rigorous scientific and analytical training is paired with extensive opportunities to apply these ideas to real-world problems. Students develop expertise in research design, data analysis, decision analysis, negotiation, and policy evaluation while working closely with faculty on hands-on projects. The major culminates in a capstone project in which students tackle an important organizational or policy challenge, integrating the analytical, behavioral, and leadership skills they have developed throughout the program. Organizations increasingly seek leaders who can combine analytical thinking with an understanding of people, incentives, and institutions. Graduates are well prepared for careers in management, consulting, strategy, public policy, government, nonprofit leadership, analytics, and many other fields, as well as graduate and professional study in business, public policy, law, economics, and related disciplines. Prerequisites All Policy and Management majors must complete mathematics and statistics prerequisites (see below), by the end of the sophomore year. Students are required to declare a concentration before their graduating semester, but are not required to choose a concentration when they initially declare (typically in the freshman or sophomore year). In fact, students are encouraged to take many of the core classes before making their concentration selection so that they can make a well-informed decision.
